ascertainment: Composite UKB registry/EHR codes and baseline self-report.
spirometry: not_applicable: the published COPD inclusion rule does not require spirometry
clinical_diagnosis: not_applicable: no independent clinical adjudication requirement
surrogate_definition: Self-reported chronic obstructive airways disease/COPD is an alternative inclusion route; no ML score is used.
subtype_secondary_phenotype: negative: no distinct COPD subtype or secondary phenotype
smoking_design: negative: no smoking restriction, stratification, or interaction reported
discovery_replication: UKB discovery GWAS; FinnGen was used for disease-level replication analyses elsewhere in the paper, but this Catalog accession is the UKB COPD scan.
overlap_notes: Probable extensive overlap with other UKB accessions. The paper analyzes cross-disease relationships, but this accession itself is a standalone COPD GWAS and must not be labeled an independent cross-disease cohort.
full_stats_status: available: GWAS Catalog full summary statistics
rationale: The accession-level statistic is binary COPD, not a shared-disease meta-statistic. Its broad rule combines coded chronic bronchitis/emphysema/COPD and self-report, so it is a mixed EHR/composite susceptibility phenotype eligible only for the secondary sensitivity stratum.
source_evidence: The Catalog reports a standalone COPD study with 27,304 cases and 430,208 controls.
Supplementary Data 31 defines UKB COPD using ICD-9 491/492/496, ICD-10 J41-J44, or self-reported chronic obstructive airways disease/COPD.
The primary methods distinguish the GWAS of nine systemic diseases from later MR and cross-phenotype analyses.
uncertainties: negative: the broad composite definition is documented; only the relative contribution of code-based versus self-reported cases is not reported
